findings.claim: OpenAI Agents Python streaming/websocket handling could treat response.failed or response.incomplete terminals carrying output as successful final responses.
primary_evidence: openai/openai-agents-python issue #3106: reporter reproduction on main commit 3854c124cb8e3e51fb660f5714405ee39ee86c5e shows a failed streamed response exposing partial output as final_output
openai/openai-agents-python PR #3107 merged 2026-05-04, merge commit 9b57f057b43d85ce695b379a7a433deb02cd1699, explicitly rejects failed/incomplete terminal payloads and adds regression tests
findings.scope: Exact to the affected OpenAI Agents Python streamed runner / Responses model websocket paths represented by issue #3106 and merged fix #3107. This is historical fixed-bug evidence, not evidence that current releases retain the defect and not a universal agent-SDK claim.

findings.claim: A retry after local-session input was durably persisted could rewind/delete that input and leave the successful assistant answer without the user turn.
primary_evidence: openai/openai-agents-python issue #3852 gives a self-contained SQLiteSession reproduction on 0.18.1: no retry -> ['user','assistant']; one retry -> ['assistant']

openai/openai-agents-python PR #3857 merged 2026-07-16, merge commit 5313a829968f18e37508b0016ec45ddde2cc8445, states streamed retries no longer rewind committed local-session input and adds regression coverage
findings.scope_correction: PR #3857 explicitly says non-streaming retry behavior remains unchanged. Therefore the verified fix and failure witness are for the streamed local Session path; do not generalize the repair to non-streaming or server-managed conversation paths from this evidence alone.

findings.claim: Celery broker redelivery of the same logical Airflow task while the original worker is still running can turn a duplicate start conflict into an authoritative failure unless the already-running identity/state is handled specially.
primary_evidence: apache/airflow issue #58441 reports Airflow 3.1.1 and 3.1.3: redelivery of the same task hits an invalid-state conflict while previous_state=running and the scheduler can mark the still-running task failed

apache/airflow PR #60855 merged 2026-03-25, merge commit f5ff9671ec81f9d259980a733766fef4c78ba91c, adds TaskAlreadyRunningError only for 409 invalid_state with previous_state=running; tests preserve generic errors for other prior states; PR text reports manual Breeze validation where the original worker continued and the redelivery no longer marked failure

apache/airflow PR #64052 merged 2026-03-26, merge commit 95fc11ed217b51e5f256cc0a4d8a389784aec81e, catches TaskAlreadyRunningError and raises Celery Ignore() so the duplicate delivery is not recorded as FAILURE; its code gates this handling on AIRFLOW_V_3_1_9_PLUS
findings.scope_correction: The evidence supports an identity-and-current-state-specific duplicate-start exception, not a rule to ignore arbitrary duplicate deliveries. The issue directly reports 3.1.1/3.1.3, while the provider-side fix is version-gated for Airflow >=3.1.9 and the core fix is milestone 3.2.0; do not summarize this as a verified all-3.1.x behavior/fix matrix without separate release/backport evidence.

phase1_implication: Three concrete historical failure classes are primary-source supported: false-success terminalization, retry deletion of already-committed run-owned input, and broker-redelivery false failure of still-running work. They support fail-closed terminal-status checks, run-owned durable-input semantics, and stable task identity plus authoritative current-state classification. They do not by themselves prove a generic exactly-once or global parity mechanism.
